# Parserino: Fast HTML5 Parser and DOM Manipulation for D

Parserino is a high-performance HTML5 parser and DOM manipulation library for the D programming language, written in pure D (no C dependencies; the tree construction is derived from Lexbor). Names and behaviour follow the DOM, HTML and Selectors 4 standards.

## Core Concepts

- **Document**: The main entry point for parsing and managing HTML content.
- **Node**: Any node of the tree (element, text, comment, doctype, document, fragment).
- **Element**: A node that is an element; it adds attributes, `innerHTML`, `matches`, ... It converts implicitly to `Node`; `node.asElement` goes back (invalid if the node isn't an element).
- **Show**: Navigation methods take a template filter of node kinds (as DOM `whatToShow`): `children!(Show.All)`, `descendants!(Show.Comment)`, `firstChild!(Show.Text)`. The default is `Show.Element`, and then the result is an `Element`.
- **Lazy Ranges**: Search and navigation ranges (`byTagName`, `bySelector`, `children`, `descendants`, ...) are lazy bidirectional struct ranges (`retro` gives reverse document order).
- **Lazy Parsing**: `Document(html, Parsing.Lazy)` builds the tree only as far as the queries need (`doc.byClass("x").take(3)` stops early). Results are identical to a full parse.
- **Errors**: searches and navigation return an invalid node (`== null`) or an empty range when nothing is found; invalid operations throw `ParserinoException`.
- **Memory**: `Document` is reference counted; each `Node` keeps its document alive. Removed nodes stay valid. Getters return `string` copies; `...View` variants return slices of the document memory.

## Installation & Basic Usage

Add `parserino` to your `dub.json` or `dub.sdl`.

```d
import parserino;
void main() {
    auto doc = Document("<html><body><p>Hello World!</p></body></html>");
    assert(doc.body.firstChild.textContent == "Hello World!");
}
```

## API Reference

### Document
- `this(string html, Parsing parsing = Parsing.Eager, size_t chunkSize = DefaultChunkSize)`, `this(string html, ParseOptions options)`: Parse; `ParseOptions` has `parsing`, `chunkSize`, `scripting`.
- `this(Snapshot)`, `snapshot`: A compact copy of the tree; `Document(snap)` rebuilds a document without parsing.
- `ctDocument!html`: Parsed at compile time; each call returns a new document rebuilt from the stored tree.
- `dup`: A deep copy.
- `finishParsing()`, `isParsing`, `bytesParsed`: Control and inspect lazy parsing.
- `documentElement`, `head`, `body` (the `<frameset>` in frameset documents), `node` (the document as a `Node`).
- `title`, `title(string)`: Get or set the document title.
- `createElement(tag)` (an `Element`), `createText(text)`, `createComment(text)` (`Node`s).
- `fragment(html, context = "body")`: Parses html in the context of an element into a `DocumentFragment` node; inserting it moves its children.
- `toString()`: Serializes the entire document back to HTML.
- **Search Methods**: `byId(id)` (an invalid `Element` if not found), `byClass`, `byTagName` (`"*"` for all), `bySelector(css or Selector)`, `byComment(text)`, `byCommentExact(text)`, `children!show`, `descendants!show`.

### Node
- `isValid`, `nodeType`, `nodeName`, `isElement`, `isText`, `isComment`, `asElement`, `ownerDocument`.
- `textContent` (get/set), `dataView`.
- Navigation (all with `!(Show...)`): `parent`, `firstChild`, `lastChild`, `nextSibling`, `previousSibling`, `children`, `descendants`; `hasChildNodes`, `contains(node)` (inclusive).
- Search: `byId`, `byClass`, `byTagName`, `bySelector`, `byComment`, `byCommentExact`.
- Mutations: `append`, `prepend`, `before`, `after`, `replaceWith` (accept a `Node`, a `string` as text, `"<b>x</b>".asFragment` as html, a fragment), `appendChild(node)`, `remove()`, `~=`.
- `dup`, `shallowDup`, `toString`.

### Element (also has all the `Node` members)
- `localName` ("div", "foreignObject"), `tagName` ("DIV"), `id` (get/set), `classes`, `attributes`.
- `getAttribute(name)` (`null` if missing), `setAttribute`, `hasAttribute`, `removeAttribute`.
- Views: `localNameView`, `idView`, `getAttributeView`, `classesView`, `attributesView`.
- `innerHTML`, `outerHTML` (get/set), `innerText` (same as `textContent`), `startTag`.
- `matches(css)`, `isEmpty` (`:empty`), `isBlank` (`:blank`), `copyFrom(e)`, `shallowCopyFrom(e)`.
- `el = "<b>html</b>";` replaces the element with the parsed one.

### Parse errors and encodings
- `ParseOptions.collectErrors` and `doc.parseErrors`: a list of `ParseError` (`code`, `line`, `column`, `name` as in the HTML standard, e.g. "unexpected-null-character"). With `ctDocument!(html, options)` the errors are compile errors.
- The input is UTF-8 (BOM removed, invalid bytes become U+FFFD). `parserino.encoding.toUtf8(bytes)` detects the encoding (BOM, `<meta charset>`) and converts UTF-16, windows-1252, ISO-8859-2, windows-1250/1251.

### Selector
- `Selector(string css)`: A compiled css selector, reusable with any document (throws `ParserinoException` on invalid syntax). `ctSelector!css` and `bySelector!css` compile it at compile time.

### Range Helpers
- `frontOrThrow(range)`: The first element; throws `ParserinoException` if the range is empty.
- `frontOr(range, fallback)`: The first element or `fallback`.
- `frontOrInit(range)`: The first element or an invalid node.

### Fragment Handling
To insert raw HTML strings as DOM nodes (instead of plain text), use `.asFragment`:
```d
doc.body.append("<p>New Paragraph</p>".asFragment);
```

## Examples
Explore the `examples/` directory for practical implementations:
- `01_hello_world`: Basic parsing and editing.
- `02_search_elements`: Using `byTagName` and CSS selectors.
- `03_edit_dom`: Adding fragments and creating new elements.
- `04_wikipedia_scraper`: Real-world scraping with lazy filtering and CSS selectors.
- `05_html_templates`: Parserino as a template engine with serverino: plain html templates (parsed at compile time with `ctDocument`) filled by id/class, cloned rows, removed sections, automatic escaping; two different layouts filled by the same code.
